# Spec review phase 6: lifecycle guards

A response that asserts progress must state what changed; a sender can withdraw its own obsolete request instead of forging recipient receipts; an intent whose holder is absent and whose base has drifted is reported stale and stops blocking present participants; and each coordination binding names its sibling so discovering one yields both.

Next action: Split COOP-3 scale and presence material out of coordination.md, dedupe the contract text it shares with cooperation-contracts.md, and split the artifact digest manifest out of the capsule.

recommended_next_action.action: Review and implement one bounded silo-v1 derivation/adoption binding with dependency, authority, shared-resource, and crash-recovery evidence; the existing COOP-1 completeness work remains open.

checkpoint.summary: Silo specification formulated in the unreleased 0.8.0 draft; normative rules and structural fixtures only. Workstate maintained through the existing local snapshot projector; no complete replay or COOP conformance claim.

do_not_assume: The AWP 0.8 draft retains a separate Coordination C0-C3 ladder
The current local tools are a complete COOP-1 binding
COOP-1 provides COOP-2 semantic awareness or integration assurance, or COOP-3 authentication, fencing, or scale
Imported authority grants external side effects
The silo specification is an implemented runtime or an operational conformance claim
Silo adoption automatically approves feature implementation or enables agent communication
handoff.requested_action: Review and implement one bounded silo-v1 derivation/adoption binding with dependency, authority, shared-resource, and crash-recovery evidence; the existing COOP-1 completeness work remains open.

read_first.statement: Define a portable workstate format for LLM session continuation and multi-agent code coordination.
Portable state must not require private chain-of-thought or hidden runtime state.

read_first.choice: Keep released artifacts and identifiers immutable; develop normative changes under spec/drafts; use minor versions for incompatible 0.x changes; publish errata or new versions rather than moving tags.
read_first.question: How should AWP distinguish released protocol semantics from development?

read_first.choice: Use no named contract for portable collaboration; COOP-1 for small-group conflict reduction, COOP-2 for semantic and integration coordination, and COOP-3 for protected scalable coordination. Consultation is an independently enabled optional subprotocol.
read_first.question: How should AWP express cooperation and coordination conformance?

read_first.statement: The AWP 0.8 draft uses a COOP-1/2/3 work-coordination ladder: COOP-1 reduces collisions through deterministic guarded work and recovery; COOP-2 adds semantic awareness and integration assurance; COOP-3 adds protected enforcement and scale. Portable collaboration needs no named contract, and consultation is optional.

read_first.mitigation: Complete an end-to-end COOP-1 work trial without consultation, then separately implement and test consultation-loop enforcement before claiming that optional subprotocol.
read_first.statement: The local prototype has guarded work, receipt-backed exit, canonical checkpoint projection, and fresh-entry integrity checks, but does not yet compose every COOP-1 work requirement in one binding or provide independent interoperability evidence. The optional consultation subprotocol has no binding-owned interaction storage, repeat-key deduplication, or loop-budget enforcement.

read_first.title: Compose and test a complete COOP-1 cooperation binding

read_first.choice: Specify silo-v1 as a Synchronization fork profile in AWP 0.8.0, with immutable single-parent ancestry, explicit base updates and local overrides, separate ownership/approval/publication, isolated resources or common atomic admission, and dependency-complete receipted adoption. Partial adoption does not close a silo; parent closure does not invalidate children. Creating a silo never enables collaboration or spending.
read_first.question: How should AWP preserve and accept alternative hierarchical project states?

read_first.mitigation: Implement and exercise the procedural cases in Silo Profile section 9 before claiming operational support.
read_first.statement: The new silo profile has structural fixtures but no runtime, cross-workstate dependency-closure evaluator, shared-resource binding, adoption publisher, or independent interoperability evidence.

resume.recommended_next_action: Review and implement one bounded silo-v1 derivation/adoption binding with dependency, authority, shared-resource, and crash-recovery evidence; the existing COOP-1 completeness work remains open.
